answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding collateral to each identity and aggregating evidence of coordinated equivocation: when k identities violate the same safety rule, the correlated penalty grows as O(k²), making a swarm costlier than isolated misconduct. Upon detection, an additional exponential multiplier in capital loss prevents splitting control across aliases from diluting risk. Across tide, zephyr, and sonnet test cases, penalties apply to the controlling stake, not merely disposable names.
